memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'You may bring them to the LORD as an offering of the firstfruits, but they are not to be offered on the altar as a pleasing aroma.'" - Lev 2:12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
So yeast and honey were not forbidden altogether. They could be brought as firstfruits — the joyful harvest gift given to God at the start of the season. They just could not go on the altar fire.

God draws a careful line. There is a place for the sweet things and the everyday things in our relationship with Him. He receives them gladly. But the altar — the place of atonement, the place where sin is dealt with — has different terms.

We sometimes blur this. We assume that because God is pleased with our giving, our service, and our good works, those things somehow contribute to our standing before Him. They do not. The altar was never about what we bring; it was about what God provides.

Paul makes the same distinction sharply: it is by grace you have been saved, through faith — and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God — not by works, so that no one can boast (Eph 2:8-9). And then, in the very next verse, he says we were created to do good works. The works are real and God delights in them. They are simply not the altar.

Bring God your firstfruits gladly. But rest your soul on Christ alone.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Am I quietly trusting my good works to contribute to my acceptance with God?
2. What good gifts can I joyfully bring to God today, without confusing them with my salvation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for receiving the gifts of my life. Keep me from ever laying them where only Christ belongs. Amen.
